newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq moves closer to renewing oil sale program.
newsitem.headline: Iraq moves closer to renewing oil sale program.

text.p: Iraq on Wednesday cleared another hurdle in resuming oil sales when U.N. oil experts sent Baghdad's new pricing plan to a Security Council panel, which has until Friday to approve or reject it.

Iraq delayed submitting the pricing formula until U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan approved Baghdad's programme to distribute the humanitarian goods bought with the oil revenues. He did so on Monday and Iraq now has to sell $1 billion in oil by Sept. 5.
An "oil-for-food" programme went into effect last December and was renewed for another six months on June 8, with oil sales divided into 90-day or three-month periods.
If the pricing plan is approved on Friday, Iraq can sign individual oil contracts. These again have to be endorsed by the U.N. oil experts or overseers, usually within 24 hours.

The oil-for-food programme allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food, medicine and other goods for its people to ease the effects of U.N. sanctions imposed seven years ago when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
"The U.N. overseers have submitted to the committee the new oil pricing formula which they received from Iraq and which will govern the sale of Iraqi oil," U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said.
The Security Council sanctions committee has 48 hours to examine the formula. If there are no objections by 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) on Friday, the prices become valid, he added.
The United Nations did not reveal the prices that have to conform to industry standards.

But industry and diplomatic sources said on Tuesday that Iraq reduced prices for Basrah Light and Kirkuk crude oil after initial objections from the U.N. overseers who conferred by telephone with officials from the Iraq State Oil and Marketing Organisation (SOMO) before the plan was submitted in writing.

Under the new rates, Basrah Light to the United States, is now priced at $4.50 under West Texas Intermediate for August on an FOB basis. Kirkuk to Europe is at Dated Brent -$1.90, and at WTI -$3.50 for the United States.
Asian customers received a price for Basrah Light at an average of Oman/Dubai -55 cents, the sources said, also on an FOB basis for August.

SOMO had first proposed a price of $4.40 per barrel under regional benchmark WTI for U.S. buyers of its Basrah Light, according to traders with oil companies that had contracts with Iraq earlier in the year.
But the traders said that Iraq's original pricing formula was too high, given a rise in freight costs in the past two months and the difficulty in marketing a large amount of Iraqi crude.
